01. Do you hold a Master's degree, Juris Doctor (J.D.), or other advanced degree in Higher Education Administration, Human Resources, Public Administration, Law, Student Affairs, Conflict Resolution, or a closely related field? Options: Yes | No
02. Using examples from your own professional experience, please explain how you developed your understanding of Title IX.

03. Please describe any progressively responsible experience that you have conducting civil rights, Title IX, and/or workplace misconduct investigations and preparing formal investigative reports. Include the total number of years’ experience and the name(s) of employer(s). If you do not possess this experience, please type “n/a”.

04. Please describe any experience that you have developing and facilitating training programs for students and/or employees on Title IX, discrimination & harassment prevention, retaliation, and equity-related topics. Include the total number of years’ experience and the name(s) of employer(s). If you do not possess this experience, please type “n/a”.

05. Please list any certifications you currently have in Title IX grievance procedures, civil rights investigations, workplace investigations, alternative dispute resolution, and/or mediation. Include the name of the certificating organization/agency, the expiration date, and be sure to upload copies of the proof of completion. If you do not have any relevant certifications, please type “n/a”.
Certifications in Title IX grievance procedures, civil rights investigations, workplace investigations, alternative dispute resolution, and/or mediation.

Bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university with major course work in human resources, organizational management, public administration, law degree, or field directly related to the major responsibilities of the position
Master’s degree or higher.

Master's degree, Juris Doctor (J.D.), or other advanced degree in Higher Education Administration, Human Resources, Public Administration, Law, Student Affairs, Conflict Resolution, or a closely related field.
Three (3) full-time equivalent years of progressive experience in Human Resources.
Three years (full-time equivalent) of civil rights investigatory experience.
Experience developing and facilitating training programs for students and/or employees on Title IX, discrimination & harassment prevention, retaliation, and equity-related topics.
Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO) and governing laws and procedures, U.S. Code. §Title VII and Title IX requirements and Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) requirements.
Pertinent federal and state laws and regulations.
Regulations pertaining to civil rights investigations and labor relations.
Receiving and responding to complaints of discrimination and working with public agencies.
Conducting investigations and closing cases.
Facilitating small group processes.
Performing detailed and time-sensitive work
Communicating with others on confidential and sensitive issues.

Objectively and effectively investigating complaints of alleged unlawful discrimination, sexual harassment, and other violations of rights relative to assigned program areas, prepare reports, and make findings and recommendations related to law and legal precedence
Interpret and apply provisions of Federal laws, Education Code, Government Code, Title V, Title IX, and other federal and state regulations as related to the responsibilities of the position.
Demonstrated knowledge of current Title IX regulations
Demonstrated understanding of and sensitivity to meeting the needs of individuals from diverse academic, socioeconomic, cultural, disability, and ethnic backgrounds.
Well-developed oral and written language skills to prepare and deliver reports and professional correspondence.
